title: Provisioner: rollback telemetry and upgrade gating for private EKS control plane
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As Redwood Private customers run EKS-based control planes in VPCs, we've seen two classes of upgrade failures: subtle config drift that manifests after a roll and transient infrastructure glitches during node replacement. The existing terraform provisioner applies upgrades but lacks robust telemetry to detect silent regressions, and there are no automated gating/rollback controls that operate at the orchestration layer. Goal: Add deterministic, low-latency telemetry hooks and gating logic into the terraform-based provisioner so an automated canary/upgrade window can (a) detect behavioral regressions quickly using health signals, (b) abort and trigger a safe rollback if thresholds are breached, and (c) capture diagnostic telemetry to S3/Datadog for postmortem and fast triage. This ticket implements the terraform module enhancements plus lightweight operator-run hooks for gating and rollback coordination.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes an optional lifecycle 'upgrade_gate' block that accepts health check endpoints, expected thresholds, and rollback policy

During a control-plane upgrade with upgrade_gate enabled, the orchestrator evaluates health signals (API server latency, kube-apiserver errors, control-plane node readiness) from a canary cluster before promoting changes to the fleet

If any pre-configured threshold is violated within the configured window, the provisioner aborts the rollout and triggers a documented, idempotent rollback plan via terraform (state-backed) and a short-lived incident ticket in PagerDuty
Telemetry artifacts (rollback snapshot, kube-apiserver logs, terraform plan/apply diffs) are uploaded to a customer-specific S3 path and linked in the generated incident
Automated e2e test verifies gating behavior in a simulated failure (API server high 5xx rate) and passes in CI
Docs: module README and runbook updated with examples, operational playbook for manual rollback, and required IAM roles
tasks: Design upgrade_gate block schema and Terraform variable names (input validation)
Implement terraform resources for canary stack and health probe IAM roles
Add a small Go-based upgrade-checker utility (container) that evaluates metrics and returns canonical pass/fail
Wire upgrade-checker into provisioner: pre-promotion hook and abort/rollback path
Add telemetry upload step: collect logs, plan/apply diffs, and push to S3 with TTL tags
Create e2e test harness in CI that exercises canary fail/pass and asserts rollback is triggered
Write runbook and module README with examples and RBAC/IAM requirements
Security review and KMS configuration for telemetry artifacts
comments: 2025-02-11 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: product agrees on minimal viable gating: API server latency (p95), control-plane node readiness ratio, and API 5xx rate. We should avoid gating on embedding jobs or long-running batch workloads.
2025-02-14 - Liam O'Connor: Initial schema proposal pushed to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-provisioner/pull/212 - requesting design review from infra and SRE

2025-02-18 - SRE (review): Suggest adding a configurable 'quarantine' window before rolling back to account for transient infra flakiness. Also recommend storing telemetry encrypted with KMS and adding explicit IAM granularities for cross-account S3 writes.

2025-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Trade-off discussion: decided not to implement live traffic mirroring for the canary in v1 to keep scope small; we'll rely on synthetic probes and health metrics. Noted for v2.
2025-02-24 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented initial upgrade-checker (go) and container image built (gcr.io/redwood/upgrade-checker:v2025-02-24). Scaffolding at tools/upgrade-checker in repo.
2025-02-27 - QA: Found a race condition when multiple provisioners run concurrently against same state; added a state-locking step and a retry backoff in the provisioner orchestration layer.
2025-03-01 - Design: README draft posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Priv+EKS+Upgrade+Gates - feedback requested from security and platform
notes: Operational constraints: module must be backward compatible with existing customers who don't opt-in. Ensure all new IAM permissions are optional and gated by a top-level boolean. Rollback must avoid destructive operations (no force-delete of PVs or stateful data).
